summary: A 1932 pole lookout on Looking Glass Mountain was succeeded by a 1958 41-foot timber tower with R-6 cab, now staffed in summer; registered on NHLR 1995.

facts.design: 41-foot wooden or treated timber tower with R-6 cab and 15 by 15 ft live-in flattop cab and catwalk (1958); first lookout a 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (1932)
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Idaho Panhandle National Forests (Priest Lake Ranger District); older sources say Kaniksu National Forest

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts describes it as drive-up and staffed in summer; staffing is seasonal and visitors may find the lookout off duty

events.note: First lookout on the summit (then Looking Glass Mountain): 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab
Kenneth Osborn named as lookout at the Looking Glass station (July 1934 newspaper item)
C.A. Stoner transferred away from Looking Glass lookout (October 1936 newspaper item)
Summit renamed Gisborne Mountain for Harry T. Gisborne (Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1949; a July 1950 newspaper item reports the national board approving the name)
Present 41-foot timber tower with R-6 cab built; NHLR gives a 15 by 15 ft live-in cab and catwalk; July 1958 newspaper item notes Fulton Messmore erecting a lookout
Registered August 1, 1995 as NHLR US 128, ID 6
Idaho Fire Lookouts post (dated January 1, 2022) says the lookout is staffed in summer; visitors found it off duty during smoke

corrections.why: The standing tower is 41 feet (about 12.5 m), per NHLR, the Idaho site and the Forest Lookouts page. 12.2 m (40 ft) matches the 1932 pole tower, not the 1958 tower the record describes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1949 for the summit rename, while a July 1950 newspaper item reports the national board approving the name that year. The story reports both dates and does not pick one.
NHLR names the Idaho Panhandle National Forests; the Idaho site, firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page use Kaniksu National Forest, the older name. Both are in the record.
NHLR gives 5,550 ft (1,692 m), matching the record's 1691.6 m. Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give 5595 ft. No change proposed.

notes_for_editor: Record height 12.2 m matches the 1932 40-ft pole tower; the standing 1958 tower is 41 ft (proposed 12.5 m). Build year: 1932 per NHLR, Idaho and Forest Lookouts; a Priest River Experimental Forest storymap appeared in search with 1933 and a 1951 rename, but its page returned no text and it was not used. Current staffing rests on a Jan 2022 Idaho Fire Lookouts post and an undated firelookout.com line (staffed in summer); no current Forest Service source was read, and a 2020 IPNF post about access limited to staffed lookout towers appeared in search but was not readable. Access level left unset because no source states public visiting rules; the record's access 'unknown' stands. Elevation and forest-name conflicts are in resolved_conflicts. Staff names come from newspaper items quoted by the Forest Lookouts and Idaho sites; no new photos were recorded.
